vc_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me choose how to form my venture capital fund's legal stack (GP LLC, Delaware LP filing, LPA, GP operating agreement, EIN, fund bank account). This is a comparison and preparation task only — the final selection is my decision.

Please research and compare fund formation options across two categories: (1) self-serve fund formation platforms designed for emerging VC managers (e.g., services like Angel List (Assure), Carta Launch, Odin, or similar fund-formation-as-a-service platforms), and (2) traditional law firms that specialize in fund formation for emerging managers. If you need clarification on my fund size, target close date, number of anticipated LPs, or budget for formation costs, ask me first, since these affect which option fits best.

For each candidate, gather and summarize: typical cost/fee structure, turnaround time, what's included (GP entity formation, LP filing, LPA and GP operating agreement drafting, EIN, bank account setup support), any minimum fund size or AUM requirements, notable limitations, and reputation/track record with early-stage fund managers (cite sources where possible).

Organize your findings into a clear comparison table (platform/firm name, cost, speed, scope of services, limitations, source links) plus a short written recommendation of 2-3 finalists with pros and cons for my situation.

Once the comparison and recommendation are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off — do not contact, engage, sign up with, or commit to any platform or law firm on my behalf. I will review your research and make the final selection myself.

vc_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the formation of the GP entity for our VC fund — either a new standalone LLC or a new designated series under our existing Delaware series LLC. Before starting, ask me for: (1) which structure we're using (new LLC vs. new series), (2) the exact legal name I want to use for the GP entity (and confirm availability if possible), (3) the registered agent name and address we'll use in Delaware, (4) the authorized organizer's full legal name and title, and (5) the fund's general management structure details needed for the formation document (e.g., member/manager info).

Once you have these, prepare everything short of filing: draft the certificate of formation (or the series designation document/amendment if we're adding a series to the series LLC) with all required fields filled in — entity name, registered agent, organizer name, effective date, and any series-specific language. Navigate to the Delaware Division of Corporations 'How to Form' page (https://corp.delaware.gov/howtoform/) and identify the correct filing path and any associated state fee, and summarize the exact steps and required fields for that submission. Also prepare a short checklist of everything I need to review or bring to signing (name, registered agent, organizer identity, fee amount, filing method).

Do not submit the filing, sign the certificate of formation, or take any action that commits us legally — the organizer's signature is a binding legal act and must remain with an authorized human, so stop for human sign-off once the draft document and checklist are ready.

Report back with: the completed draft certificate/series designation text, the identified filing fee and submission path, and the review checklist, clearly labeled as pending human signature and submission.

vc_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the Delaware Certificate of Limited Partnership for our new venture fund, ahead of filing with the Delaware Division of Corporations (https://corp.delaware.gov/howtoform/). This is a policy-gated legal step: you must prepare everything but stop for human sign-off before any execution or submission occurs.

First, ask me for any of the following if I haven't already provided them:
- The exact legal name of the fund (the LP), confirming it's available and compliant with Delaware naming rules (must include an LP designator like 'L.P.' or 'Limited Partnership').
- The name and address of the General Partner entity (the GP LLC or GP series) that will sign the certificate.
- The name and address of the Delaware Registered Agent we'll use for the fund.
- The effective date of formation, if not simply the filing date.

Using this information, draft the Certificate of Limited Partnership content in the standard Delaware format (fund name, registered office/agent, GP name and address, and any other statutory required fields), and prepare a checklist covering: (1) confirming name availability, (2) confirming registered agent engagement, (3) the draft certificate text ready for GP review, and (4) the Delaware filing portal steps and fee amount so I know what to expect when I file.

Do not submit the filing, do not attempt to sign or attest on the GP's behalf, and do not enter payment or execute anything in the Delaware portal — the GP's signature/attestation on this certificate is a legal act that remains a human step and requires a human to execute.

When done, report back: the drafted certificate text, the completed checklist, any open questions (e.g., name conflicts), and a clear note that the document is ready and awaiting GP signature and manual filing — stop for human sign-off at that point.

vc_001:n3b.prompt:
You are helping me track receipt of the stamped Delaware Certificate of Limited Partnership for our new VC fund's LP entity. The actual arrival and issuance of the stamped, file-marked certificate by the Delaware Division of Corporations remains a human step — you cannot make the state process or return it faster, and there is no interface to drive for this part.

What I need you to do instead:

1. Ask me for: the fund LP's exact legal name, the date we (or our registered agent/formation counsel) submitted the Certificate of Limited Partnership filing, and the name of the registered agent or law firm handling the filing on our behalf, if I haven't already given you these.
2. Prepare a simple tracking checklist/log entry noting: filing date, expected turnaround (standard Delaware LP processing time, or expedited if we paid for it), registered agent/counsel contact, and a due date for follow-up if nothing arrives.
3. Draft a polite status-check email (do not send it) addressed to our registered agent or formation counsel, asking whether the stamped LP certificate has been received back from the Delaware Division of Corporations, for me to review and send myself.
4. Once I confirm the stamped certificate has arrived (I will tell you or share the document), record receipt: note the file-stamp date, the LP's file number as shown on the certificate, and confirm the entity name matches exactly what we intended.
5. Flag this as the trigger to proceed to the next legal-stack steps (EIN application, bank account opening) but do not start those yet.

Done looks like: a clear tracking log with filing/expected dates, a ready-to-send status-check draft, and — once I confirm receipt — a recorded confirmation of the stamped certificate's file number and date for our records.

Report back with: the tracking checklist, the drafted status-check email, and (after I confirm arrival) a short confirmation summary of the certificate's details. Do not attempt to contact the Delaware Division of Corporations or submit anything on my behalf — just prepare materials and stop for human sign-off before any email is sent.

vc_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a simple Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) for a new Delaware venture fund. This is a drafting/preparation task only — a human must review and sign off before anything is executed or filed.

First, ask me for any of these inputs you don't already have: (1) the fund's exact legal name and the GP entity's exact legal name, (2) state of LP formation (assume Delaware unless told otherwise), (3) target fund size and minimum LP commitment, (4) management fee percentage and step-down schedule if any, (5) carried interest percentage and any hurdle/preferred return, (6) fund term and extension provisions, (7) key terms like GP capital commitment, recycling provisions, key-person provisions, and (8) the name of outside fund counsel if one has been engaged.

Using this information, draft a plain-language, simple LPA covering: parties (GP and LPs), purpose and term, capital commitments and drawdowns, allocations and distributions (including waterfall), management fee and carry mechanics, GP duties and indemnification, transfer restrictions, key-person and removal provisions, dissolution, and standard boilerplate (governing law, amendments, notices). Clearly flag every section as a draft and mark any placeholder numbers or terms that still need confirmation.

When the draft is complete, prepare a summary checklist of open items (fee/carry terms, LP commitment amounts, counsel review) that need my decision or confirmation, and note that outside counsel should review the document for legal sufficiency before it is used.

Do not send this document to any LP, counsel, or counterparty, and do not treat it as final or binding. After preparing the draft and checklist, stop for human sign-off. Report back with the draft LPA text, the list of open items, and any assumptions you made in filling gaps.

vc_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the GP Operating Agreement for the general partner entity of my new venture fund. Before drafting, ask me for any of the following you don't already have: the GP entity's legal name and state of formation (Delaware LLC or a series of an existing series LLC), the names and ownership/voting percentages of all members/managers, the management structure (member-managed vs. manager-managed and who the manager is), capital contribution amounts and timing for GP members, how management fees and carried interest will be allocated among GP members, decision-making and voting thresholds for major actions (e.g., admitting new members, dissolving the GP), transfer restrictions, indemnification provisions, and the fund name and Delaware LP entity it will manage.

Using this information, draft a complete GP Operating Agreement covering: formation and purpose, membership interests and capital contributions, allocations and distributions (fees/carry), management authority and voting rules, indemnification and liability limitations, transfer restrictions, withdrawal/removal provisions, and dissolution terms. Where legal or tax nuances require it (e.g., carry waterfall mechanics, clawback provisions), flag them clearly as items for review by fund counsel rather than guessing at language.

Produce the draft as a clean document plus a short summary memo listing key terms and any open questions or assumptions you made. Do not finalize, sign, file, or send this agreement anywhere — after preparing the draft and summary, stop for human sign-off. Report back with the draft agreement, the summary memo, and a checklist of any missing information or decisions I still need to confirm before the agreement can be executed.

vc_001:n5b.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for the General Partner's signature on our venture fund's Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) and GP Operating Agreement. This is a legal execution step that only the authorized GP signatory can complete, but I need you to get everything ready beforehand.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: the current final drafts (or draft locations) of the LPA and GP Operating Agreement, the legal name of the GP entity, the full legal name and title of the authorized signatory, the fund's Delaware LP name/file number, and which e-signature service we use (e.g., DocuSign, Adobe Sign, HelloSign) if any.
2. Review both documents for completeness: confirm all signature blocks, dates, entity names, and defined terms are consistent between the LPA and Operating Agreement, and flag any blank fields, mismatched party names, or missing exhibits/schedules.
3. Prepare a signing checklist listing: documents to be signed, signatory name/title, order of execution, and any counterparty signatures still needed (e.g., LPs, other GP members).
4. If we use an e-signature platform, prepare the envelope/request (upload documents, set signer fields and routing) via the dashboard, but do not send it or trigger the signing yet.
5. Summarize any open legal issues, inconsistencies, or missing information you find, and note who should confirm them (e.g., fund counsel).

Done looks like: both documents are fully reviewed and internally consistent, a signing checklist is prepared, and (if applicable) the e-signature request is drafted and staged but unsent.

Important: Do not sign, approve, submit, or send the documents for execution yourself. This step requires the GP's personal legal authority and must stop for human sign-off. Report back with the checklist, any flagged issues, and confirmation that the documents are staged and ready for the GP's review and signature.

vc_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the IRS Form SS-4 application to obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) for our new venture fund's Delaware LP entity. This is the online IRS EIN application at https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/get-an-employer-identification-number — note there is no API for this; the SS-4 wizard must ultimately be submitted by a human.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for any missing inputs needed to complete the SS-4: the fund's exact legal name (as filed with Delaware), the Delaware LP formation date and state, the entity's mailing address, the type of entity (limited partnership), the reason for applying (started new business), the fund's principal business activity, the expected number of employees (likely zero), and the closing month of the fund's accounting year.
2. Ask me who the designated 'responsible party' is — this must be a natural person with authority over the entity (typically the GP's authorized signatory) — and confirm their name, title, and SSN/ITIN will be provided directly by that person (do not ask me to paste their SSN/ITIN to you; note where it will need to be entered).
3. Draft a complete, field-by-field pre-fill of the SS-4 form data based on the above, organized so it can be copied directly into the IRS online wizard.
4. Prepare a short checklist confirming: entity name matches Delaware filing exactly, responsible party info is ready, and all fields are internally consistent.
5. Do NOT submit the application, attest to any information, or click through the IRS wizard's final certification — the responsible party must review and submit it themselves, since IRS rules require their personal certification under penalty of perjury.

When the draft and checklist are ready, present them to me clearly and then stop for human sign-off, noting that final submission remains a human step.

vc_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me prepare and submit the fund bank account application for our newly formed VC fund GP entity, using {{vendor}} (a startup-banking platform) as the account provider. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in our records or configured credentials, including: the fund's legal entity name (GP LLC and/or fund LP), state of formation, EIN (once issued), formation documents (certificate of formation, LP agreement, GP operating agreement), registered agent details, principal business address, and the names/titles/ownership percentages of all beneficial owners and authorized signers (25%+ owners plus any control person). 

Actions to take:
1. Gather and organize all the above entity and ownership details into a clean summary document.
2. If {{vendor}} is Ramp, use the Ramp CLI's applications resource to submit/apply for a new bank account application, populating all required entity, ownership, and signer fields from the gathered information.
3. Attach or reference the formation documents and EIN confirmation as required by the application.
4. Prepare a checklist of any identity verification or beneficial-ownership certification documents the authorized signer will need to personally upload or certify (e.g., government ID, ownership certification form), since this cannot be completed on my behalf.
5. Once the application is submitted, monitor and report the application status when asked.

What done looks like: the application is fully filled out and submitted (or staged and ready for submission) with all entity/ownership data included, supporting documents attached where possible, and a clear checklist of remaining identity/ownership certification items that require the authorized signer's own action.

Important: You must not certify beneficial ownership, verify identity, or approve/sign anything on my behalf — this remains a human step. Prepare everything needed, then stop for human sign-off. Report back with the application status, a summary of what was submitted, and the outstanding certification checklist.
